title: CHAPTER FORTY. On the humans obligation to death
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): whose equity stands as out from guilt, but whose infliction stands as out from ye affection belonging toward vengeance or ye wrath plus rigor belonging toward justice, that same which stands as joined with Gods truth in keeping ye threat — unless it stands as tempered by means belonging toward new grace, by means belonging toward that same which eternal curse stands as turned into eternal blessing joined with temporary chastisement — and out from ye affection belonging toward vengeance plus out from guilt or obligation to punishment follows ye punishment itself. by means belonging toward that same which God seeks to assign to ye sinner toward ye evil belonging toward fault ye evil belonging toward punishment — from offense there stands as born in God ye affection belonging toward avenging. that same which has before it Gods prohibition plus ye denunciation belonging toward punishment if ye human should not obey Gods law — this obligation presupposes partly Gods offense out from sin. From chapter 37, aphorism 2, it stands as plain that same after ye dogma belonging toward ye permission belonging toward sin there stands as place toward ye doctrine belonging toward ye fallen humans obligation to death or ye undergoing belonging toward punishment, belonging toward that same which Genesis 2:17 speaks. into that same which by means belonging toward ye just judgment belonging toward God offended by means belonging toward that same fall he has been reduced, so that same he stands as liable to eternal curse — the OBLIGATION belonging toward ye human to death stands as his penal condition. Thus far concerning ye permission belonging toward sin: On ye humans obligation to death. CHAPTER FORTY.
pass_b_english: CHAPTER FORTY. On the humans obligation to death.

Thus far concerning the permission of sin: the OBLIGATION of the human to death is his penal condition, into which by the just judgment of God offended by that fall he has been reduced, so that he is liable to eternal curse. From chapter 37, aphorism 2, it is plain that after the dogma of the permission of sin there is place for the doctrine of the fallen humans obligation to death or the undergoing of punishment, of which Genesis 2:17 speaks.

This obligation presupposes partly Gods offense from sin, which has before it Gods prohibition and the denunciation of punishment if the human should not obey Gods law. From offense there is born in God the affection of avenging, by which God seeks to assign to the sinner for the evil of fault the evil of punishment. And from the affection of vengeance and from guilt or obligation to punishment follows the punishment itself, whose equity is from guilt, but whose infliction is from the affection of vengeance or the wrath and rigor of justice, which is joined with Gods truth in keeping the threat — unless it is tempered by new grace, by which eternal curse is turned into eternal blessing joined with temporary chastisement.
source_text: CAPUT QUADRAGESIMUM, De obligatione hominis ad mortem. HAec de permissione peccati: OBLIGATIO hominis ad mortem est eius poenalis conditio, in quam Dei lapso illius offensi iusto iudicio redactus est, ut maledictioni aeternae sit obnoxius. Ex capitis 37 aph. 2 patet, post dogma de permissione peccati locum esse doctrinae de obligatione hominis lapsi ad mortem seu poenae subitionem, de qua Gen. 2:17. Supponit autem haec obligatio partim offensionem Dei ex peccato, quod ante se habet Dei prohibitionem ac poenae denunciationem, siquidem homo legi Dei non obediret. Ex offensione nascitur in Deo affectus vindicandi, quo videlicet Deus appetit peccatori pro malo culpae tribuere malum poenae. Ex vindictae vero affectu et reatu seu obligatione ad poenam sequitur ipsa poena, cuius aequitas ex reatu, inflictio vero ex affectu vindictae seu ira et rigore iustitiae, quae coniungitur cum veritate Dei in servanda comminatione, nisi temperetur nova gratia, qua maledictio aeterna vertatur in benedictionem aeternam coniunctam cum castigatione temporaria.
